title: The first dragon volvelle (lunar latitude: Caput and Cauda Draconis), from Astronomicum Caesareum
maker: Petrus Apianus (Peter Apian), with Georg Apian; printed, hand-coloured and assembled in the Apians' workshop
medium: Hand-coloured woodcut on paper, with a cut paper disc turning on the plate
source: National Library of Poland (Polona, object 149346690), via Wikimedia Commons; public domain
derived_from: components/dragon-volvelle/assets/plate.webp, ring.webp and disc.webp (the 1600 px cut of the 3840 px scan; see that folder's credits.json and tools/)
note: The button's roundel: the paper disc and the ring of the mater it turns on, cut round on the outer rule of the printed zodiac (781.5 px on the 1600 px plate, about the mater's printed centre) and scaled to 384 px across by one premultiplied Lanczos resample (tools/face.py). face.webp is the plate itself inside that circle, the disc at home; ring.webp is dragon-volvelle's restored mater (the annulus the turning disc can uncover, restored there from the same printed signs a third or a sixth of the way round); disc.webp is dragon-volvelle's paper disc with its two tabs, CAPVT and CAVDA, and the shadows they cast. Nothing drawn or recoloured. volvelle.json is the geometry in face pixels.

title: Fonts (demo only)
notes: demo.html sets its words in Inter and Cormorant Garamond from Google Fonts (SIL Open Font License 1.1). The button itself uses the page's --sans.

title: References (not used as images)
notes: Lars Gislén, 'A commentary on the volvelles in Petrus Apianus' Astronomicum Caesareum' (2018), the Latitude of the Moon: one disc on the mater with tabs CAPVT and CAVDA, year marks and the arched latitude scales.
Library of Congress, Bibliomania, 'Dragons in the Astronomicum Caesareum' (2025): Apian coloured, cut and assembled the instruments himself; the layers are tied together at the centre.
